title: Chords and Tangents of a Circle
seo_title: Chords and Tangents – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use the properties of chords and tangents: perpendicular from the centre, equal chords, tangent and radius, tangents from a point, alternate segment. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on chords and tangents: perpendicular bisectors of chords, equal chords, tangents from an external point and lengths. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A tangent meets the radius at 90°
key_sub: Two tangents from one point are equal.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The perpendicular from the centre to a chord cuts the chord in half.
  • A tangent is at right angles to the radius at the point of contact.
  • The two tangents from an outside point are equal in length.

Examples

Example

r = 5 cm, distance of chord from centre 3 cm

Half chord = √(25 − 9) = 4

Answer: Chord = 8 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to double the half chordThe perpendicular gives half the chord.
Missing the right angleRadius ⟂ tangent.
Using Pythagoras without a right angleFind the 90° first.

What is the alternate segment theorem?
faq.a: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. OM is perpendicular to the chord AB, OM = 4 cm and the radius is 5 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(5² − 4²) = √9 = 3 cm, so AB = 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. OM is perpendicular to the chord AB, OM = 6 cm and the radius is 10 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8 cm, so AB = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. OM is perpendicular to the chord AB, OM = 30 cm and the radius is 34 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(34² − 30²) = √256 = 16 cm, so AB = 2 × 16 = 32 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 32 cm is 12 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 16 cm. Radius OB = √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 16 cm is in a circle of radius 17 cm with centre O. Find the distance OM of the chord from the centre.
items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 8 cm. OM = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 42 cm is 20 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 21 cm. Radius OB = √(20² + 21²) = 29 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 6 cm is 4 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 3 cm. Radius OB = √(4² + 3²) = 5 cm.

items.q: A chord of length 9 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. Find its distance from the centre, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Half the chord is 4.5 cm. Distance = √(10² − 4.5²) = 8.9 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 12 cm is 8 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 6 cm. Radius OB = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 24 cm is in a circle of radius 13 cm with centre O. Find the distance OM of the chord from the centre.
items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 12 cm. OM = √(13² − 12²) = 5 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 32 cm is in a circle of radius 20 cm with centre O. Find the distance OM of the chord from the centre.
items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 16 cm. OM = √(20² − 16²) = 12 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 30 cm is in a circle of radius 17 cm with centre O. Find the distance OM of the chord from the centre.
items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 15 cm. OM = √(17² − 15²) = 8 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 84 cm is in a circle of radius 58 cm with centre O. Find the distance OM of the chord from the centre.
items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 42 cm. OM = √(58² − 42²) = 40 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 20 cm is 24 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 10 cm. Radius OB = √(24² + 10²) = 26 cm.

items.q: A chord AB of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre O. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: MB = 8 cm. Radius OB = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm.

items.q: Complete the statement: The line joining an external point to the centre of the circle …
c: bisects the angle between the two tangents from that point
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: the line joining an external point to the centre of the circle bisects the angle between the two tangents from that point.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 26 cm. AB = CD = 48 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(26² − 24²) = 10 cm.

items.q: In a circle with centre O, chord AB = 4 cm and chord CD = 40 cm. Which chord is closer to O?
c: You cannot tell without the radius
They are the same distance from O
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: Complete the statement: The perpendicular bisector of a chord …
c: is equal in length to the chord
passes through the centre of the circle
is a tangent to the circle
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre of the circle.

items.q: Complete the statement: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord …
c: bisects the angle at the centre only when the chord is a diameter
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: the perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. AB = CD = 12 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm.

items.q: In a circle of radius 58 cm, chords PQ and RS are both 40 cm from the centre. PQ = 84 cm. What is RS?
items.e: Chords the same distance from the centre are equal: RS = 84 cm.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. AB = CD = 16 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(10² − 8²) = 6 cm.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 34 cm. AB = CD = 32 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(34² − 16²) = 30 cm.

items.q: In a circle of radius 17 cm, chords PQ and RS are both 8 cm from the centre. PQ = 30 cm. What is RS?
items.e: Chords the same distance from the centre are equal: RS = 30 cm.

items.q: In a circle with centre O, chord AB = 4 cm and chord CD = 60 cm. Which chord is closer to O?
c: They are the same distance from O
You cannot tell without the radius
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: In a circle with centre O, chord AB = 10 cm and chord CD = 24 cm. Which chord is closer to O?
c: You cannot tell without the radius
They are the same distance from O
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: Complete the statement: Two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point …
c: meet the circle at the ends of a diameter
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are equal in length.

items.q: In a circle with centre O, chord AB = 4 cm and chord CD = 36 cm. Which chord is closer to O?
c: You cannot tell without the radius
They are the same distance from O
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 13 cm. AB = CD = 24 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(13² − 12²) = 5 cm.

c: You cannot tell without the radius
They are the same distance from O
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: Complete the statement: A tangent to a circle …
c: is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact
cuts the circle at two points
is parallel to the radius at the point of contact
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 26 cm. AB = CD = 20 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(26² − 10²) = 24 cm.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 50 cm. AB = CD = 96 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(50² − 48²) = 14 cm.

items.q: Complete the statement: Two equal chords in the same circle …
c: are the same distance from the centre
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: two equal chords in the same circle are the same distance from the centre.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 56°. Find ∠TAB.
items.e: TA = TB, so △TAB is isosceles: ∠TAB = (180° − 56°) ÷ 2 = 62°.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 10 cm and TA = 24 cm. Find OT.
TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 12 cm and TA = 16 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 90°. Find ∠AOB.
items.e: ∠OAT = ∠OBT = 90°. The angles of quadrilateral OATB add up to 360°, so ∠AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 90° = 90°.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 10 cm and OT = 26 cm. Find the length of TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(26² − 10²) = 24 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 80°. Find ∠TAB.
items.e: TA = TB, so △TAB is isosceles: ∠TAB = (180° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 50°.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 40 cm and TA = 42 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 16 cm and OT = 20 cm. Find the length of TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(20² − 16²) = 12 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 84°. Find ∠TAB.
items.e: TA = TB, so △TAB is isosceles: ∠TAB = (180° − 84°) ÷ 2 = 48°.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from the point T to a circle. TA = 12 cm. What is TB?
items.e: Tangents from an external point are equal in length: TB = 12 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 8 cm and TA = 6 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents from the point T to a circle. TA = 5 cm. What is TB?
items.e: Tangents from an external point are equal in length: TB = 5 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 16 cm and TA = 30 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 4 cm and OT = 5 cm. Find TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(5² − 4²) = 3 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 3 cm and OT = 5 cm. Find TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. TA = 3 cm and OT = 5 cm. Find the radius.
TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 12 cm and OT = 20 cm. Find TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(20² − 12²) = 16 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. TA = 8 cm and OT = 10 cm. Find the radius.
TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. TA = 12 cm and OT = 15 cm. Find the radius.

A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. AB = 13 cm, BC = 12 cm, CD = 7 cm. Find DA.
items.e: Tangents from each vertex are equal, so AB + CD = AD + BC. DA = 8 cm.

items.q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. AB = 12 cm, BC = 10 cm, CD = 14 cm. Find DA.
items.e: Tangents from each vertex are equal, so AB + CD = AD + BC. DA = 16 cm.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 21 cm, BC = 13 cm and CA = 12 cm. Find the length of the tangent from B to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 21, y + z = 13, z + x = 12, so x + y + z = 23 and the tangent from B is 11 cm.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 21 cm, BC = 19 cm and CA = 20 cm. Find the length of the tangent from B to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 21, y + z = 19, z + x = 20, so x + y + z = 30 and the tangent from B is 10 cm.

items.q: A parallelogram circumscribes a circle. What kind of parallelogram must it be?
items.e: AB + CD = AD + BC and opposite sides are equal, so 2AB = 2BC: all sides are equal. It is a rhombus.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 13 cm, BC = 10 cm and CA = 7 cm. Find the length of the tangent from B to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 13, y + z = 10, z + x = 7, so x + y + z = 15 and the tangent from B is 8 cm.

items.q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. AB = 10 cm, BC = 10 cm, CD = 5 cm. Find DA.
items.e: Tangents from each vertex are equal, so AB + CD = AD + BC. DA = 5 cm.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 15 cm, BC = 13 cm and CA = 20 cm. Find the length of the tangent from C to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 15, y + z = 13, z + x = 20, so x + y + z = 24 and the tangent from C is 9 cm.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 9 cm, BC = 13 cm and CA = 12 cm. Find the length of the tangent from A to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 9, y + z = 13, z + x = 12, so x + y + z = 17 and the tangent from A is 4 cm.

items.q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. AB = 11 cm, CD = 17 cm, DA = 15 cm. Find BC.
items.e: Tangents from each vertex are equal, so AB + CD = AD + BC. BC = 13 cm.

items.q: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB, BC and CA. AB = 18 cm, BC = 11 cm and CA = 15 cm. Find the length of the tangent from C to the circle.
items.e: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, C be x, y, z: x + y = 18, y + z = 11, z + x = 15, so x + y + z = 22 and the tangent from C is 4 cm.

items.q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. BC = 11 cm, CD = 11 cm, DA = 8 cm. Find AB.
items.e: Tangents from each vertex are equal, so AB + CD = AD + BC. AB = 8 cm.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 3 and OP = 5. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(5² − 3²) = 4.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 6 and PA = 8. Find OP.
items.e: OA ⟂ PA, so OP is the hypotenuse: √(6² + 8²) = 10.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = x + 7 and PB = 3x − 15. Find PA.
items.e: Tangent segments from one point are congruent: x + 7 = 3x − 15, so 2x = 22 and x = 11. PA = 18.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = 21. Find PB.
items.e: Two tangent segments from the same outside point are congruent: PB = PA = 21.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = 23. Find PB.
items.e: Two tangent segments from the same outside point are congruent: PB = PA = 23.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 8 and OP = 17. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(17² − 8²) = 15.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 9 and PA = 12. Find OP.
items.e: OA ⟂ PA, so OP is the hypotenuse: √(9² + 12²) = 15.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = 15. Find PB.
items.e: Two tangent segments from the same outside point are congruent: PB = PA = 15.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. TA = 8 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 6 × 8. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48 cm².

items.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 16 cm and 12 cm are drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm, on the same side of the centre. Find the distance between the chords.
items.e: Distances from the centre: √(10² − 8²) = 6 and √(10² − 6²) = 8. On the same side, subtract: 2 cm.

items.q: A tunnel is shaped like part of a circle of radius 13 m. The floor is a horizontal chord 24 m wide. How high is the highest point of the tunnel above the floor, if the centre is above the floor?
items.e: The centre is √(13² − 12²) = 5 m above the floor, and the top is one radius above the centre: 5 + 13 = 18 m.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 4 cm. TA = 3 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 4 × 3. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 4 × 3 = 12 cm².

items.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 10 cm and 24 cm are drawn in a circle of radius 13 cm, on opposite sides of the centre. Find the distance between the chords.
items.e: Distances from the centre: √(13² − 5²) = 12 and √(13² − 12²) = 5. On opposite sides, add: 17 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 8 cm. OT = 17 cm. Find the perimeter of the kite OATB.
items.e: TA = TB = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm and OA = OB = 8 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (8 + 15) = 46 cm.

items.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 30 cm and 16 cm are drawn in a circle of radius 17 cm, on the same side of the centre. Find the distance between the chords.
items.e: Distances from the centre: √(17² − 15²) = 8 and √(17² − 8²) = 15. On the same side, subtract: 7 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 7 cm. TA = 24 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 7 × 24. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 7 × 24 = 168 cm².

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 4 cm. OT = 5 cm. Find the perimeter of the kite OATB.
items.e: TA = TB = √(5² − 4²) = 3 cm and OA = OB = 4 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (4 + 3) = 14 cm.

items.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 10 cm and 24 cm are drawn in a circle of radius 13 cm, on the same side of the centre. Find the distance between the chords.
items.e: Distances from the centre: √(13² − 5²) = 12 and √(13² − 12²) = 5. On the same side, subtract: 7 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 8 cm. TA = 15 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 8 × 15. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 8 × 15 = 120 cm².

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 25 cm and 7 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(25² − 7²) = 24 cm. Chord = 48 cm.

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 82 cm and 18 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(82² − 18²) = 80 cm. Chord = 160 cm.

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 41 cm and 9 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(41² − 9²) = 40 cm. Chord = 80 cm.

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 17 cm and 15 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(17² − 15²) = 8 cm. Chord = 16 cm.

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 26 cm and 10 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(26² − 10²) = 24 cm. Chord = 48 cm.

items.q: Two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point P. If ∠AOB = 120°, find ∠APB.
TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. OT = 5 cm. Find the perimeter of the kite OATB.
items.e: TA = TB = √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm and OA = OB = 3 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (3 + 4) = 14 cm.

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm. Chord = 8 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. TA = 4 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 3 × 4. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 3 × 4 = 12 cm².
